written_from: IBM z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385) and z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, read by section, not page (page numbers are not cited): the DD statement DSNAME parameter (generation data group relative numbers), the DISP parameter (normal / abnormal-termination dispositions, PASS), the EXEC COND parameter, and DFSMS 'Generation data groups' (relative generation resolution at job start, roll-in at job end, LIMIT). The expected answers were written before any evaluator ran on them.
scenario_input: catalog (or catalog_from: another scenario's catalog_after): per GDG base, limit and the cataloged absolute generations, oldest first. given: per step that starts, {rc: n} or {abend: code}.
scenario_answer: expect: per STEP.DDNAME of each step that runs, the absolute generation number the DD names. catalog_after: per base the cataloged generations, oldest first, after the job ends.
flow_jcl: //* #8413 slice 3: GDG relative generations. Which absolute generation
//* each DD names, and the catalog after the job. The answers are in
//* scenarios.json, written from IBM's z/OS MVS JCL Reference
//* (SA23-1385) and z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets before any

scenarios.basis: DSNAME, generation data group: (0) is the most recent generation cataloged, (-1) the one before it, (-2) the one before that. With generations 5, 6, 7 cataloged, (0) = 7, (-1) = 6, (-2) = 5. Reading creates nothing, so the catalog is unchanged.

DSNAME: (+1) names the next generation, 8. Every relative number in a job is resolved against the catalog as it stood when the job started, so (+1) in the later step C2 is the same generation C1 created, while (0) is still 7 and (-1) is still 6 (the new generation is not rolled into the catalog until the job ends). At job end 8 is cataloged as the most recent.
A later job sees the catalog the earlier job left: 8 is now (0), 7 is (-1), 6 is (-2).

DSNAME: (+1) is the next generation after the one current at job start (2), so 3; (+2) is the one after that, 4. A later step naming (+1) or (+2) names those same generations; (0) is still 2. Both are cataloged at job end, oldest first.

DISP, abnormal-termination disposition: EOUT is DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE) and E1 abends, so generation 8 is deleted and never cataloged; the PAY.GDG catalog is unchanged. E2 (COND=EVEN) runs after the abend and ends normally, so its (+1) of AUD.GDG, 3, is cataloged.

DISP: when the abnormal-termination disposition is omitted the system applies the normal-termination one. FOUT is DISP=(NEW,CATLG) and E2 abends, so generation 3 is cataloged anyway. E1 ends normally, 8 is cataloged.
EXEC COND: B1 ends RC 8, so (4,LT,B1) is true and B2 is bypassed; a bypassed step allocates none of its DDs, so BOUT creates nothing. B3's (+1) is 8 and is cataloged at job end.
DISP PASS: the generation created by P1 is passed to P2 under the same (+1) name; P2's DISP=(OLD,CATLG) catalogs it, so 8 is cataloged.

Generation data group LIMIT: the group holds at most LIMIT generations (3). Rolling 8 in makes the oldest, 5, drop out of the catalog; whether 5 is also scratched (deleted) depends on the group's SCRATCH / NOSCRATCH attribute and is not answered here. Relative numbers in the job are unchanged by the limit.

assumed.text: A new generation is rolled into the catalog at the end of the job, not at the end of its creating step (deferred roll-in); the answers for (0) / (-1) after a (+1) in the same job depend on it.

A generation whose creating step abends under (NEW,CATLG,DELETE) is not cataloged, and under (NEW,CATLG) is, per the DISP text; the absolute number is still consumed by that job only (the next job reuses it).

refused.construct: two steps of one job creating the same (+n) with DISP=NEW
refused.why: the second allocation names a dataset that already exists; IBM's text for the failure is not answered here

refused.construct: a (+n) read before any step creates it, or (0) / (-n) with no such cataloged generation
refused.why: a JCL or catalog error, not a step-flow answer

refused.construct: a PASSed generation never received by a later step
refused.why: the manual's disposition of an unreceived passed dataset is not answered here

refused.construct: DISP=(NEW,KEEP) or UNCATLG generations, absolute names (G0007V00), roll-in of EMPTY / SCRATCH groups, DISP=MOD (+1)
